text_blocks.snippet: Yes, walking can be beneficial for some people with COVID-19, but it's important to exercise caution and listen to your body. Moderate walking can help improve symptoms for many, but rest is crucial if you're experiencing severe symptoms.

list.title: May ease symptoms:
list.snippet: Exercise, including walking, can sometimes help open nasal passages and potentially improve overall well-being during a mild COVID-19 infection.

list.title: May reduce risk of long COVID:
list.snippet: Studies suggest that regular exercise, even before or after a COVID-19 infection, might help reduce the risk of developing post-acute COVID syndrome (long COVID).

list.title: Listen to your body:
list.snippet: If you have a fever, body aches, fatigue, or other significant symptoms, rest is more important than exercise.

list.title: Reduce intensity and duration:
list.snippet: If you're feeling up to walking, reduce the intensity and duration compared to your normal routine.

list.title: Avoid strenuous exercise:
list.snippet: Avoid strenuous exercise, especially if you have symptoms "below the neck," such as chest congestion, hacking cough, or an upset stomach.

list.title: Be mindful of contagiousness:
list.snippet: If you're still contagious, avoid group activities and crowded places while walking to minimize the risk of spreading the virus.

list.title: Consult with a doctor:
list.snippet: If you have any concerns about exercising while ill, it's always best to consult with a healthcare professional.
